source_caption:
📺 ER (1994–2009)

ER follows the dedicated doctors, nurses, and medical staff working in the emergency room of Chicago’s County General Hospital as they face life-threatening emergencies and difficult decisions every day. From devastating accidents and complicated surgeries to emotional patient stories, the team must work under intense pressure while trying to save lives. Alongside unforgettable characters like Dr. Mark Greene, Dr. Doug Ross, and Dr. John Carter, the series explores complicated relationships, personal struggles, and the sacrifices that come with working in medicine. Filled with powerful performances, dramatic rescues, and heartfelt moments, ER captures the challenges of healthcare while celebrating compassion, teamwork, friendship, and the extraordinary dedication of medical professionals.

🎭 Genre: Medical Drama • Romance • Drama

⭐ IMDb: 7.9/10

⏱️ Runtime: Approximately 44 minutes per episode • TV-14

🎥 Creator: Michael Crichton

🏆 Awards: Winner of 23 Primetime Emmy Awards, including Outstanding Drama Series.

📺 Where to Watch: Hulu and HBO Max in the United States. Availability varies by region.

source_details.synopsis: ER is an American medical drama television series created by Michael Crichton that aired on NBC from September 19, 1994, to April 2, 2009, with a total of 331 episodes spanning 15 seasons. It was produced by Constant c Productions and Amblin Television, in association with Warner Bros. Television. ER follows the inner life of the emergency room (ER) of Cook County General Hospital, a fictionalized version of the real Cook County Hospital, in Chicago, and the various critical professional, ethical, and personal issues faced by the department's physicians, nurses, and staff.
